wins.claim: KerfDesk drives Marlin and Smoothieware first-class with genuine dialect handling (M400 settle, comma-status fallback, fractional-S rescale); the grbl-only senders gSender and XCS have no non-grbl firmware at all and Easel only a token OEM export (+5 vs Easel, +4 vs LaserGRBL). Caveat: simulator-verified only, open A.3.3, still trails LightBurn (8).

KerfDesk ships a real 12-entry machine-profile catalog with typed evidence badges and a start-gate cross-checking declared bed/feed against live $130/$131/$110/$111 (evidence: stronger than LightBurn); LaserGRBL ships no catalog at all (+1 vs gSender). Caveat: loses to LightBurn (9) and MillMage (8), ties XCS/Easel (6).

gaps.claim: No usable DSP/Ruida support -- the .rd export is experimental, file-only and never accepted by real hardware; the whole CO2/DSP laser segment is unserved. ADR-097-recorded scope limit (not a severity bump). P1 for a DSP buyer, P2 for KerfDesk's diode/grbl-centric persona.

12 profiles with no RESEARCH_LOG provenance, a guessed .lbdev import schema (A.4.5) and no app-level saved-machines list (A.4.2), vs LightBurn auto-identify + importable manufacturer bundles and MillMage's searchable machine DB (-2 vs MillMage). P2.

grblHAL/FluidNC are thin driver deltas and the FluidNC console still accepts numeric $N=value writes with no prepareConsoleCommand guard (A.3.9) -- the catalog even claims this is 'blocked in-app' when it is not (un-ADR'd safe-handling divergence, severity-relevant). P2.

Sophisticated 7-step wizard held back by two open defects (A.3.3 unsafe streamingMode path; A.4.3 old machine numbers under a newly-picked profile name) and zero runtime/hardware verification of the $$ read/write-verify flow (-1 vs MillMage). P2.

notVerified: No fidelity (SS5.3) and no hardware (SS5.4 [HW]) categories exist in S16; every score is a plain capability rating with no PERC cap and no '*' design-intent stars. Several KerfDesk cells lean partly on [HW-CLAIMED] catalog evidence (Falcon A1 Pro grblHAL 'hardware-verified') that is CLAIMED per the repo ledger, not re-verified, and does not raise any score.

16.1: no real-hardware grblHAL/FluidNC behavior; the FluidNC 'simulator' is the GRBL sim with a FluidNC banner; whether a real FluidNC $$ dump includes $30/$32 (which the power-scale gate depends on) is unproven. The A.3.9 missing-console-guard was code-confirmed this audit; its real-controller effect was not.

16.2: all real-hardware Marlin/Smoothieware behavior -- both are simulator-verified only per ADR-095/096 ('NOT hardware-verified'). Stock Smoothie comma-vs-pipe status unconfirmed; a real Marlin's reaction to a stray override byte unconfirmed; the A.3.3 streamingMode-mismatch is a designed-open path, not exercised on hardware.

16.3: no real Ruida controller has accepted KerfDesk output (experimental everywhere); no LightBurn/MeerK40t reference .rd in the tree to diff against -- the golden test proves byte-stability, not protocol correctness; Min==Max power on a real DSP unverified; UDP transport deliberately not built.

16.4: vendor bed dimensions for xTool D1 Pro / Sculpfun S30 / Ortur LM3 / Falcon / Neotronics not verified (no network); the real .lbdev format is unknown (no genuine sample; importer parses a guessed schema); whether .lfmachine.json still drops baudRate/cameraAlignment (A.4.8) not re-checked; Falcon 'hardware-verified' claim taken from evidence text.

16.5: hardware-gated per ADR-092 -- that the wizard reads $$ correctly on a real GRBL connect, that writing $30/$32 verifies via re-read, and that the chosen origin corner flips Y correctly in emitted G-code are all unverified; wizard runtime UI not exercised (no dev-server interaction per collaboration rule 4); cited controller vitest suites not re-run this session.

Both sides documentary/code, never hands-on. Every competitor cell is [OFF]/[COMM]; no [HANDS]. MillMage rated at stable 0.8.02 and treated as competing fully in this device sector per its vendor pack despite being CNC-only (its 16.3=0 reflects that a CNC app drives no laser DSP). [INF] secondary cites (LaserGRBL grblHAL/FluidNC first-class scope; XCS software scope; XCS/Easel/gSender DSP absence) are NOT load-bearing -- no win/lose bullet rests on an [INF] cell; every win-anchoring competitor cell is [OFF].
